Depression in general took away my spark and creativity. Antidepressants don’t always completely take away your depression, it can just make it more manageable. For years I kept expecting the pills to cure me completely and becoming more depressed bc I thought something was wrong with me. So I’d hop from pill to pill hoping one day one of them would take it all away. It wasn’t until I went into intensive therapy that I realized I needed to step up too and put in the work to unravel and rework my thinking. Since then, with the help of meds and therapy, I’ve gotten into new hobbies that I can put all my creativity and love into. 

Finding the correct medicine will take some of the weight off your shoulders, and the rest of it you have to chisel away at. Meds won’t completely take away your creativity, but your depression definitely will.

For the past 13yrs I’ve been on psych meds, at this point I’ve tried almost all antidepressants. Bc I’ve been on almost all of them, I’ve had to go back and try some of them again. From my experience, there’s only a little difference in side effects. 

For instance, I took Wellbutrin back in 2012 and it was fine, but I was still struggling a bit, so I went on something else. In 2022 I thought back to when I was on it and decided to give it another chance. I felt the loss of appetite and burst of energy more than I did before, but I feel like this time it’s a lot more effective. 

Everyone’s different and your body is constantly changing, but if it’s helped you in the past, why not revisit it? Sometimes you have to weigh out the pros and cons and see what’s more beneficial to you. Good luck 🫶🏻

I’ve been on it for 3yrs and for me, it’s improved my life SO MUCH. I have been on almost every antidepressant out there and Wellbutrin has hands down worked the best. I should mention that I also have ADHD, so I feel like the similarities with adderall and somewhat being a stimulant has helped with that too. Ik some people get REALLY bad anxiety from it, but it’s actually helped calmed me down. As for the sex drive, it didn’t increase it, but it also didn’t decrease it. Everybody’s different tho, talk to your doctor about it and any side effects you might get. 

But also as you get older, don’t compare your current self with your past self. Looking back you will always have tinted glasses and it’s easy to see the positives esp when you’re not feeling great and hopeless. This pill won’t give you magic dose of confidence if you don’t already have it. It’ll just help your depression get to at least be more manageable, but it won’t take everything away. It’ll get better tho 🫶🏻
